profile_text.body:
Databricks, founded in 2013 and headquartered in San Francisco, California, describes itself as a unified data and AI platform for enterprises. Its platform is built around what it calls a "lakehouse" architecture, combining data storage, analytics, ETL, data warehousing, and AI development in a single governed environment. The company positions its platform as capable of running both analytical and operational workloads without requiring data to be copied between systems.

Databricks tracks two principal AI products. DBRX is an open-source large language model built on a Mixture-of-Experts architecture, aimed at enterprise training and general-purpose use. On the data and analytics side, the broader Databricks AI offering includes MLflow for governance, Unity Catalog for data governance and lineage tracking, and Databricks Genie, a conversational analytics interface that allows business users to query enterprise data in plain language without SQL or coding. The company also offers Lakebase, described as merging the developer experience of Postgres with lakehouse-scale analytics, and Unity Gateway, a governance and cost-control layer for managing access and observability across AI agents, models, tools, and MCPs.

The held facts show 139 instances of legal exposure recorded under California jurisdiction, though no specific cases are detailed in the available data. Databricks operates as a for-profit startup and maintains a tracked presence on theworldofai.org. No SEC filings, patents, or MCP server registrations are recorded in the current data.
